summary: Rejected on three substantive source-privacy defects: source-bearing diagnostic callers truncate before the new recorder boundary can inspect complete inputs; summary expiry/rejection discards original lineage and allows stale text to receive newer clocks, including unbound Activity saved-state restoration; normal benign voice exact prompts are falsely excluded because trusted runtime epoch metadata is scanned as card numbers. Exact commit/tree/spec binding, allowed 14-path scope, frozen files and original 36 journey bodies/assertions/order were independently verified. Direct storage sanitization preserves IDs and action success/count and current typed request still reaches generation, but these findings prevent acceptance. No Kotlin, JVM/native or Android verification is claimed.

findings.detail: R1: wrap() lines 110-120 scans only its already-assembled entry, not the complete original source. Existing callers in conversation/ConversationRuntime.kt lines 175, 263, 279, 617, 736, 851-861 and 877-883 apply prompt.take(500/1000) and generated.text.take(4000) before calling this boundary; JarvisRuntime.kt line 1078 similarly truncates heard.text. For example a source beginning "tiny ", followed by >2000 benign characters and ending "password: tiny" is excluded by history, but the normal Turn/Turn failed diagnostic retains the first 1000 source characters including tiny because the exclusion marker has already been dropped. Thus the required complete-source, whole-affected-payload exclusion is bypassed despite direct-recorder tests passing. Keep current request available, but make persistence conditional on full-source provenance: within the existing allowed paths, add an enforceable recorder-level trusted envelope/source decision or fail closed on known truncated/unprovenanced source-bearing diagnostic envelopes. Do not simply whitelist marker-shaped arbitrary text or weaken the frozen exact benign prompt contract.

R2: SummaryPreferences.getString() lines 35-38 and rejected writes lines 51-56 erase both payload and original timestamp. A subsequent stale/reworded write after sourceTimestamp() advances then sees previous=null and receives the newer history clock. Concrete boundary sequence: write S with source=1000; at 1000+RETENTION_MS read S (removed); advance source to now; write S or a rewording; it is accepted until now+90 days. The added test only retries with source still 1000 and misses this case. Runtime does not bind its captured_at to the actual summary text either: JarvisRuntime.kt lines 109-124 accepts any in-memory summary when a nonzero stored clock is eligible, while MainActivity.onCreate lines 125-128 can restore a different savedInstanceState summary without provenance. A stale bundle can therefore inherit a newer saved summary clock. Retain durable original-lineage/tombstone information through rejection/expiry and bind any restored/re-summarized capsule to its contributing source provenance; unknown stale capsules must fail closed. Do not refresh provenance merely from the current eligible history.

R3: Normal voice onPromptSubmitted lines 782-792 always adds VoiceSessionController.contextProvenance(), whose callStartedAtMs/oldestEntryAtMs/newestEntryAtMs are ordinary 13-digit epoch milliseconds. DiagnosticRecorder.wrap scans that combined envelope with MemoryArchivePolicy’s bare 13-19 digit card regex, so even a completely benign voice prompt is replaced by EXCLUDED. Exempting only the outer atMs header in readSafe() does not fix write-time rejection. This regresses the required within-window exact benign diagnostic prompt persistence on the real voice path; the new real-epoch test only tests the recorder’s own header. Separate structured trusted recorder/runtime metadata from arbitrary source text and scan the complete source fields, or omit this metadata at the allowed Runtime caller. Never broadly treat user-controlled atMs-like text as trusted metadata.
